root_cause.text: In `btrfs_ioctl_space_info()` in the Btrfs ioctl path, a TOCTOU race exists between the initial count of block-group space-info entries and the later fill/copy phase, so concurrent block group removal can make `alloc_size` larger than the number of initialized entries and cause `copy_to_user()` to leak uninitialized heap data.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message says the function “has a TOCTOU race between two passes over the block group RAID type lists,” with `groups_sem` released between passes; the second pass may fill fewer entries than counted, yet the original code copied `alloc_size` bytes. The patch changes `kmalloc` to `kzalloc` and, crucially, changes `copy_to_user()` from `alloc_size` to `space_args.total_spaces * sizeof(*dest_orig)`, confirming the bug was over-copying beyond the actually initialized data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the space info buffer in btrfs ioctl handling to avoid uninitialized memory use or data leakage.
intent_record.what: In btrfs_ioctl_space_info(), the allocation of `dest` was changed from `kmalloc(alloc_size, GFP_KERNEL)` to `kzalloc(alloc_size, GFP_KERNEL)`.
intent_record.how: The buffer `dest` is now zero-initialized when allocated, so any fields or padding not explicitly written later will start as zero instead of containing uninitialized memory. This can prevent leaking stale data or relying on garbage contents during ioctl handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix copy_to_user() in btrfs_ioctl_space_info() to use the actual space entry count when copying results to userspace.
intent_record.what: The third argument to copy_to_user() was changed from alloc_size to space_args.total_spaces * sizeof(*dest_orig), and the call was reformatted across two lines.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now copies exactly the number of bytes corresponding to the total number of space info entries being returned, instead of using the previously allocated buffer size. This aligns the user copy length with the actual data count and avoids copying an amount based on allocation sizing.

Fix copy_to_user() in btrfs_ioctl_space_info() to use the actual space entry count when copying results to userspace.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is leaking uninitialized heap data in btrfs_ioctl_space_info() when fewer entries are filled than counted. Zero-initializing the space info buffer directly mitigates that leak by ensuring any unfilled portion copied to userspace contains zeros instead of stale heap data.

The change directly addresses the described TOCTOU bug in btrfs_ioctl_space_info() by ensuring copy_to_user() uses the actual initialized space entry count, preventing copying of uninitialized heap data.

candidates.rationale: This copies the full precomputed alloc_size to userspace even though concurrent block-group removal can reduce the number of initialized space_info entries. As a result, copy_to_user() may transmit uninitialized heap bytes beyond the valid entries.
The buffer is allocated without zero-initialization, so any portion not filled before copy_to_user() can contain stale heap data and be leaked if alloc_size exceeds the number of initialized entries.

vuln_statements.explanation: This copies the entire precomputed alloc_size to userspace even when concurrent block-group removal causes fewer space_info entries to be initialized, allowing uninitialized heap data to be leaked.
The buffer is allocated without zero-initialization, so any bytes not written during the fill phase remain stale heap data and can be exposed if copy_to_user() uses the larger alloc_size.

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/ioctl.c b/fs/btrfs/ioctl.c
index 38a68863390a..4329
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet already contains the post-fix buffering and bounds checks, so the vulnerable construct is not present. It first counts entries under RCU (`list_for_each_entry_rcu(info, &root->fs_info->space_info, list) slot_count++;`), then allocates a buffer of `alloc_size = sizeof(*dest) * slot_count`, and during the second pass it prevents overrun with `if (slot_count == 0) break; slot_count--;` before `memcpy(dest, &space, sizeof(space));`. This replaces the old direct `copy_to_user()` inside the RCU loop with `memcpy()` into kernel memory and a single final `copy_to_user(user_dest, dest_orig, alloc_size)`, which is the fix for the TOCTOU/uninitialized heap leak issue. There is no remaining path where a larger `alloc_size` can lead to copying uninitialized entries to userspace in this function body.
